item.description: The post Sustaining Service Journalism in the Bay Area appeared first on Cityside Journalism.

item.title: Oaklandside's Ashley McBride wins CA School Board Association's 2024 Golden Quill award – Cityside Journalism
item.description: The award, from a group representing nearly 1,000 educational agencies across California, “recognizes the essential role journalists play in increasing understanding of public schools.”

item.title: Two Nosh stories honored at SF Press Club Awards – Cityside Journalism
item.description: East Bay Nosh stories about the Dungeness crab industry and the chef who keeps more than 600 students fed at UC Berkeley’s International House were honored at the 2024 awards gala.

item.title: Veteran investigative editor Esther Kaplan joins The Oaklandside – Cityside Journalism
item.description: Kaplan brings extensive editorial leadership experience and a passion for developing journalists to serve Oakland’s diverse communities.

item.title: The Oaklandside launches weekly podcast about Oakland news
item.description: Oaklandside 510, a new podcast from the independent, nonprofit Oaklandside newsroom, is whole new way to get Oakland news.

item.title: SPJ honors Cityside audience editor with 'Unsung Hero' award
item.description: Alejandra Armstrong's work at Cityside helps Richmondside, Berkeleyside, The Oaklandside, and East Bay Nosh reach more people.

item.title: Felicia Mello, a Berkeley High and Cal grad whose investigative reporting for CalMatters drove statewide change, will report on UC Berkeley and other East Bay colleges now under threat.
item.description: Berkeleyside is delighted to welcome Felicia Mello, a skilled reporter with a track record doing accountability work that drives statewide change, into our newsroom to cover this challenging new beat. Her first day was Nov. 17.

item.title: Berkeley library foundation honors Cityside as champion of local journalism and all things literary – Cityside Journalism
item.description: The Berkeley Public Library Foundation praised Berkeleyside’s publisher for its “outstanding contribution to our literary and civic landscape,” giving Cityside an award named for Fred and Pat Cody, founders of Cody’s Books.

item.title: The Oaklandside wins prestigious award for advancing press freedom and government transparency – Cityside Journalism
item.description: The newsroom earned the James Madison Freedom of Information award for exposing systematic violations of open records laws by city officials and challenging Alameda County’s sideshow spectator ban.

item.title: Oaklandside’s Ashley McBride, Callie Rhoades receive First Amendment award – Cityside Journalism
item.description: The pair are being honored by the First Amendment Coalition with its Free Speech and Open Government Award for their reporting last year on the lead crisis in Oakland public schools.
